problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 & -7 \\ 12 & -8 & 6 \\ 12 & -10 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

The vector $v$ and the matrix $A$ are given above. 
If $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2,$ then what is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$

feedback.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}10 & -7 & -3 \\ 8 & -5 & -3 \\ 10 & -8 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vector $v$ and the matrix $A$ are given above. 
If $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2,$ then what is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =2.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}10 & -7 & -3 \\ 8 & -5 & -3 \\ 10 & -8 & -2\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -7 & -3 \\ 8 & -7 & -3 \\ 10 & -8 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}8{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 8{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 10{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -7 & -3 & 0 \\ 8 & -7 & -3 & 0 \\ 10 & -8 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{5}{4}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}8 & -7 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{4} & -\frac{1}{4} & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}8 & -7 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{4} & -\frac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{1}{8}(7{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{8}(7(\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3})+3{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{1}{3}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=3,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{2}{1}=2.$
